name: Bonner & Associates

summary.text: Bonner & Associates is a Washington grassroots-lobbying firm. In 2009, working as a subcontractor to the Hawthorn Group on behalf of the American Coalition for Clean Coal Electricity (ACCCE), it sent letters to members of Congress opposing the Waxman-Markey climate bill, some of which falsely purported to come from groups such as a local NAACP branch and an American Association of University Women branch. The House Select Committee on Energy Independence and Global Warming held a hearing on October 29, 2009.

facts.claim: ACCCE paid the Hawthorn Group nearly $3 million in 2009 for outreach to minority, senior, business and veterans' groups, and Hawthorn in turn hired Bonner & Associates to gather letters from those groups.
facts.quote: Hawthorn in turn hired Bonner and Associates to drum up letters from those groups.

sources.title: Coverage of the October 29, 2009 House hearing on forged letters (Bonner & Associates / ACCCE)

facts.claim: The AAUW testified that a Bonner employee resurrected a defunct Charlottesville AAUW branch, used the AAUW logo and delivered a letter to a Virginia congressman; Bonner told the AAUW that 58 letters were sent on ACCCE's behalf, as many as 13 of them fraudulent.
facts.quote: a total of 58 letters were sent to several members of Congress by Bonner & Associates on behalf of ACCCE; as many as 13 of which were fraudulent

facts.claim: ACCCE acknowledged that Bonner worked on its behalf as a Hawthorn subcontractor and said it had not known about or condoned the forged letters.
facts.quote: ACCCE said it didn't know about the fake letters beforehand, or condone them.

sources.title: Coverage of the October 29, 2009 House hearing on forged letters (Bonner & Associates / ACCCE)

facts.claim: ACCCE said it learned of the forged letters on June 24, 2009, two days before the House passed the climate bill; the affected members were not told until after the vote.
facts.quote: ACCCE said it was made aware of the forged letters on June 24, 2009—a full two days before the House narrowly passed the climate bill.

sources.title: Coverage of the October 29, 2009 House hearing on forged letters (Bonner & Associates / ACCCE)

facts.claim: The House Select Committee hearing was first postponed after ranking member Jim Sensenbrenner objected that witness testimony had not been provided 48 hours in advance; ACCCE president Joe Miller testified on October 29, 2009.
facts.quote: The delay came after Ranking Minority Member Jim Sensenbrenner (R-Wisc.) raised concerns that the committee had not been provided with witness testimony 48-hours in advance.

openQuestions: Site claim (documented; forged letters to three House Democrats, posing as NAACP, Hispanic community group and AAUW): the AAUW letter and the ACCCE/Hawthorn chain are supported. The NAACP and Hispanic-group letters and the count of three House Democrats were not confirmed from the sources used.
No source found on any legal consequence for Bonner & Associates.
